_: Vellus hair: fine, short, unmedullated, lightly pigmented down on the face and body (K1, K2). One keratin fibre (cuticle of 4-8 scale layers over the cortex), at ~20-25 C and 50-65 % RH unless a state says otherwise. Contact is fibre-on-fibre: nothing passes through anything; strands touch at the fibre radius, slide with the scale or catch against it, and lock together by capillary bridges when wet or oiled. Eye-and-hair materials lane, 2026-11-07. Lies near the skin; reads as a soft sheen/peach fuzz, moves with skin contact rather than gravity (EI ~1e-11 N m2).

alpha.src: HAIRMD T7: measured specular FWHM 9-10 deg -> lobe sd 3.8-4.3 deg -> beta_m ~0.08-0.1 (R34); used as the GGX-like width of the R lobe; pbrt 'typical' 0.25 is ~3x wider

n.src: HAIRMD T7: eta 1.55 (pbrt typical, Blender default; keratin 1.55-1.56)

cuticle_tilt_deg.src: HAIRMD T7 (R34 goniophotometry); KINDS_HEAD: 2.7-3.4 deg D from 0.5 um step over 8.3-10.7 um scale interval

model.v: Marschner / Chiang hair BSDF (R, TT, TRT lobes shifted +2a, -a, -4a)

absorption.v: melanin per hair diameter: pbrt sigma_a RGB black 3.35/5.58/10.96, brown 0.84/1.39/2.74, blond 0.06/0.10/0.20; Chiang eumelanin 0.506/0.841/1.653, pheomelanin 0.343/0.733/1.924

translucency.v: blond and grey fibres pass light (TT, TRT strong); black nearly opaque per fibre

static.src: ANON_E: static ~1.6x the kinetic values below (fibre static/kinetic ratios); a 2008 sliding-angle test gave hair-on-hair static ~0.5 virgin, 0.6-1.1 treated (search summary, weak); wet x1.9 and oiled x0.75 as kinetic

kinetic.src: ANON_E from measured anchors: single fibre on polyamide 0.13 dry / 0.25 wet (DEWRI25), on hard rubber 0.18-0.26 (SCOTT80); against-scale 1.23x to > 2x with-scale (WEIAND25), 1.7x taken; wet = dry x 1.9 (DEWRI25 ratio); oiled / conditioned >= 25 % lower than clean (BOWEN16); vellus assumed as scalp keratin (no data)

friction.counterface: hair on hair (the pair table carries comb, skin, cotton, silk); 'with scale' = sliding toward the tip, 'against' = toward the root

load_dependence.v: mu falls as load rises (fibre thins and flattens; more so wet)

speed_dependence.src: SCOTT80 (vs hard rubber): rises with speed

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: NEUMANN from the water contact angles below (CA_SCC12, CA_RSC22); 18-MEA keeps virgin hair low-energy

capillary_bridge_uN_per_crossing.src: PHYS F = 4 pi R gamma cos(theta), R = 10 um, gamma water 72, sebum ~30 mN/m (E), cos(theta) = 1 upper bound (receding angle on a wet fibre is low)

tack.v: dry: none; wet: bundles coalesce (elastocapillary); sebum raised fibre withdrawal force 2-8x (1 % synthetic sebum)

restitution.src: not found and not meaningful for a fibre: a hair has almost no mass; collisions are damped by bending and air drag (see solver.impact)

water_contact_angle_deg.src: CA_SCC12 (Wilhelmy, single fibres); CA_RSC22 (native Mongolian 97.0, bleached 62.5)

oil_contact_angle_deg.src: sebum and cosmetic oils spread on keratin (they wick along fibres and into bundles: STYLING P56, P58); 0 taken

water_absorption.src: STYLING P29/P46 (Robbins via Lab Muffin) and D12

swelling_on_wetting.src: STYLING P60 (diameter ~15 %); length 1-2 % is E (keratin fibres swell far more across than along: Robbins & Fernee 1983 qualitative)

oil_absorption.v: coconut, olive, sunflower oil diffuse into the fibre (bridges fade); mineral oil stays on the surface

triboelectric.v: positive end of the series, just below human skin: hair charges + against comb plastics (PE, PP, PVC, PTFE, hard rubber) and silk/cotton are close to neutral against it; nylon sits near hair (small charge)

combing_charge_vs_RH.v: falls linearly from 20 to 50 % RH; above ~60 % RH static fly-aways vanish
combing_charge_vs_RH.src: LUNN77 (the >60 % clause is E from the regain curve)

resistivity_ohm_m.src: not found for hair as numbers; keratin (wool) falls ~0.3 decade per % water content (wool 3e12 ohm cm at 7 % water to 6e6 at 25 %, search summary, unverified); with hair's regain curve (STYLING D12) this gives the values to an order of magnitude; E: recalled, not re-read

charge_decay_s.v: log half-life linear in RH (20-50 %): seconds to minutes in dry winter air, sub-second above ~60 % RH
charge_decay_s.src: LUNN77 gives the linear-log law; magnitudes E

permittivity_rel.src: keratin/wool dielectric constants ~3-6 rising with water (recalled textile data, not reopened)

hardness.src: not found as a hardness number for hair (nanoindentation exists; not read)

abrasion.v: cuticle flattens at 10 mN, wears and lifts at 100 mN over 10^4 crossed-fibre cycles; lifted scales make friction direction-dependent

collision_thickness_mm.src: fibre radius d/2 = 20/2 um (minimum separation between centrelines = d)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: upper bound: axial E 3.1 GPa / d; the transverse modulus of hair was not found (lower). In practice: treat the fibre as incompressible across and use an IPC barrier at d_hat = 0.1 r

ramp.src: IPC barrier keeps centrelines >= d apart (no pass-through), friction from the lagged normal force

contact_damping_ratio.src: keratin loss factor ~0.1 at low frequency (fibre DMA, recalled) -> zeta ~ tan(delta)/2; E: recalled, not re-read

restitution.src: not meaningful: momentum is carried by the bending wave, not a bounce

response_time_ms.src: PHYS first bending period of a free 0.175 cm end (min of 5 cm and the typical length; E 3.1 GPa, d 20 um): how fast a struck hair answers; scales with L^2

wave_speed_m_s.src: PHYS sqrt(E/rho), sqrt(G/rho) with E 3.1 GPa, G 1.0 GPa (HARPER07 at ~50 % RH)

damping_ratio.src: as contact_damping_ratio; air drag dominates for free hair

fibre_fibre_friction_kinetic.src: as contact.friction.kinetic (anchors DEWRI25, SCOTT80, WEIAND25, BOWEN16)

direction_rule.v: the 'against' value applies when the contact point moves toward the ROOT of the fibre being rubbed (its scale edges face the tip); each fibre carries its root-to-tip tangent; two fibres crossing in opposite orientations both see 'against' in one of them

bundle_contact.v: strands in a lock lie near-parallel and touch along lines, not points: use segment-segment line contact with friction along the axis (the directional pair) and across it (the 'with' value). Dry locks hold by entanglement and the against-scale catch; wet and oiled locks are held by capillary bridges (per crossing values above) and coalesce elastocapillary into clumps (mean clump ~0.67 of the largest stable one); conditioner lowers friction and packs locks ~15 % denser

packing_fraction.src: geometry: random loose hair is mostly air; aligned wet locks approach hexagonal packing (0.907 limit); no measurement found

model.src: Cosserat / discrete elastic rod: stretch, bend (two axes for an elliptic section), twist

density_kg_m3.src: JSCC82 re-read 11-08 (J Soc Cosmet Chem 33(2), 1982, Table V, 21 C, six tresses): hair fibre density 1.32 +/- 0.005 g/cm3 at 0 and 12 % RH, 1.34 at 44 %, 1.36 at 65 %, 1.32 at 75-85 %

diameter_um.src: KINDS_VB: facial 16 um (forehead), trunk/limb < 30 um by definition; 20 a middle value

length_mm.src: KINDS_VB: cap 0.5-2 mm face (fit), ~3 mm trunk (D)

E_GPa.src: SAYAHI16 tensile 3.1 +/- 0.16; MAMADA07 bending ~10 GPa (bundles); wet = dry / 2.5 is D from MATRIX21 (dry 2-3x wet) - carried from scalp hair (KINDS_VB T6 does the same)

shear_GPa.src: HARPER07 torsion pendulum (>1.5 at <=10 % RH to ~0.7 at 90 %); RH_50 interpolated (D); in water ~0.1 is E (keratin fibres lose about an order of magnitude of torsional rigidity when soaked: wool data, recalled)

bending_stiffness_EI_Nm2.src: PHYS EI = E pi d^4/64 at d 20 um; ellipse a/b 1.1 at equal area (I = pi a b^3/4); wet: d x1.15, E/2.5. Which E to use: tensile 3.1 matches single-fibre sag (hair.md), bending 10 GPa is the bundle test; choose by the look of a hanging lock

torsion.src: PHYS GJ, J = pi d^4/32, G 1.0 GPa dry (50 % RH), 0.1 GPa wet

radius_cm.src: not found; near straight over 1-2 mm (KINDS_VB)

gravity_length_cm.src: PHYS (EI/(rho A g))^(1/3), E 3.1 GPa: a free end shorter than this barely sags

yield_strain_pct.src: Robbins' tensile curve of keratin fibres (Hookean to ~2 %, yield plateau to ~25-30 %, post-yield to break), recalled, not reopened

elastic_recovery.src: STYLING P37: healthy hair stretches ~20 % dry, ~50 % wet and recovers fully (salon test)

set_glass_transition_C.src: STYLING section 4 (Tg climbs as it dries: why hair keeps the shape it cools in)

break_strain_pct.src: SAYAHI16 47 +/- 4 % dry; DEWRI25 cites strain to 52 %; wet 50-60 is E (keratin breaks at higher strain when wet, recalled)

xpbd_bend_compliance_per_Nm2.src: 1/EI (round, E 3.1 GPa); divide by segment length per the XPBD rod formulation

xpbd_stretch_compliance_per_N.src: 1/(E A): effectively inextensible; use a hard length constraint

segment_length_mm.src: a few segments per gravity length / per curl turn; curl needs >= 8 segments per turn

conductivity_W_mK.src: keratin/wool fibre ~0.2 W/mK (recalled textile value; a hair mass is far lower, mostly air); E: recalled, not re-read

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: dry keratin ~1.3-1.6 kJ/kgK (recalled); water raises it; E: recalled, not re-read

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) of the solid fibre

emissivity.src: organic dielectric in the thermal IR (typical 0.9-0.97)

denature_C.src: STYLING (iron temperature row: keratin denatures ~233 C; damage from 130-170 C repeated)

wet.src: MATRIX21 (E / 2-3), STYLING P60 (d +15 %), P29 (+30 % mass), DEWRI25 (mu x1.9); density 1.32 x 1.30 / (1.15^2 x 1.015); water coat darkens (STYLING wet row)

oiled.src: BOWEN16 (>= 25 % lower mu with sebum), STYLING P56 (film > 0.5 um hides the scale steps: mirror-like), P58 (bridges, withdrawal force x2-8); n of sebum from oil.sebum

product.src: conditioner/silicone: combing work -85 %, volume -15 % (STYLING D13, P57); lowers the direction difference (scales smoothed) - values E; grit/texture spray is the opposite (friction up): STYLING P59

KINDS_VB.cite: The project's research note hair_kinds_vellus_body.md: K1-K5 body kinds

KINDS_AP.cite: The project's research note on hair kinds (underarm and lower body): AP1, AP4, AP10, T5

STYLING.cite: The project's research note hair_styling.md: D12 regain (Robbins via P29), P43 Bico 2004 elastocapillary, P46 porosity, P56 oils, P57 conditioner, P58 sebum, P60 wet swelling, P37 elasticity, shrinkage table
STYLING.lic: project record; underlying trade and journal sources as listed there

SAYAHI16.cite: Sayahi E et al. Int J Cosmet Sci 38:470 (2016) (hair.md R22): E 3.1 +/- 0.16 GPa, stress at break 201 MPa, strain 47 %
SAYAHI16.lic: paywalled; numbers used as facts (read via hair.md)

MAMADA07.cite: Mamada A, Nakamura K. J Cosmet Sci 58(5):485 (2007) (hair_kinds_head K19): bending modulus ~10 GPa, 50-fibre bundles, women < 40
MAMADA07.lic: SCC library; abstract read; numbers used as facts

DEWRI25.cite: Dewri SP, Gnanamoorthy R. Investigation on the friction coefficient of Indian-origin human hair. Tribology in Industry 47(2):326-332 (2025): single fibre on polyamide capstan, steady mu 0.13 +/- 0.02 dry, 0.25 +/- 0.03 wet; mu falls with load; cites Lee & Kwon Poisson 0.37 +/- 0.05, strain to 0.52
DEWRI25.lic: open access journal (licence line not found in the PDF text); numbers used as facts

SCOTT80.cite: Scott GV, Robbins CR. Effects of surfactant solutions on hair fiber friction. J Soc Cosmet Chem 31(4):179-200 (1980): capstan vs hard rubber, dry mu seldom > 0.2; 0.18 / 0.24 / 0.26 at 1 / 9 / 22 in/min
SCOTT80.lic: SCC online library, free page view; numbers used as facts

KONNO24.cite: Konno S, Asanuma K, Nonomura Y. Friction dynamics of straight, curly and wavy hair. J Oleo Sci 73 (2024): probe toward the root 0.47 / 0.51 / 0.54; finger model on bundles mu_k 0.67 (straight), 0.64 (curly), stick-slip against the cuticle
KONNO24.lic: J-STAGE open access, licence not checked; abstract numbers used as facts

BOWEN16.cite: Bowen J, Johnson SA, Avery AR, Adams MJ. Friction and wear of human hair fibres. Surf Topogr Metrol Prop 4:024008 (2016): crossed fibres, 18 C 40-50 % RH; sebum or conditioner >= 25 % lower initial mu than hexane-cleaned; direction dependence after cuticle lifting (~1000 cycles)
BOWEN16.lic: all rights reserved (abstract only read); numbers used as facts

WEIAND25.cite: Weiand E, Rodriguez-Ropero F, Roiter Y, Angioletti-Uberti S, Dini D, Ewen JP. Understanding and controlling the friction of human hair. Adv Colloid Interface Sci 345:103580 (2025): anisotropic friction from cuticle edges interlocking root-ward; 18-MEA loss raises friction; tip-to-root mu > 2x root-to-tip in Robbins' data, 23 % in high-load capstan data (as read in search summaries of the review)
WEIAND25.lic: CC BY 4.0 (full text not reached; abstract and summaries only)

HARPER07.cite: TRI/Princeton single-fibre torsion pendulum studies, J Cosmet Sci 57-58 (2006-2007; library.scconline.org v057n05, v058n04): untreated hair shear modulus > 1.5 GPa at <= 10 % RH falling to ~0.7 GPa at 90 % RH; G' 1.58 GPa (22 % RH), cortex ~0.6 GPa
HARPER07.lic: SCC library; numbers read in search summaries; used as facts

MATRIX21.cite: 'The matrix revisited', J Cosmet Sci 72 special edition (library.scconline.org v072nSE): dry Young's modulus 2-3x the wet one; modulus falls with RH
MATRIX21.lic: SCC library; number read in a search summary; used as fact

CA_SCC12.cite: J Cosmet Sci 63(1) (2012), Wilhelmy contact angles on single fibres: virgin 88 +/- 2 deg, 18-MEA stripped 83 +/- 2, bleached 78 +/- 1, bleached + conditioner 83.5
CA_SCC12.lic: SCC library; numbers read via a search summary

CA_RSC22.cite: Open-access hair-surface wetting study (RSC Soft Matter 2022 d1sm01720a or PMC8991896, CC BY): native Mongolian hair 97.0 +/- 1.7 deg, bleached 62.5 +/- 0.8; cos theta linear in sulfonate coverage
CA_RSC22.lic: CC BY 3.0/4.0 (which of the two articles carries the numbers not verified)

LUNN77.cite: Lunn AC, Evans RE. The electrostatic properties of human hair. J Soc Cosmet Chem 28:549-569 (1977): combing charge falls linearly 20-50 % RH; log charge half-life linear in RH; quats cut charge mainly by lubrication
LUNN77.lic: SCC library; trends used as facts

TRIBO.cite: Triboelectric series (AlphaLab 2009 table and its secondary copies, 72 F 35 % RH): human hands/skin at the positive end, human hair just below; most plastics (PE, PP, PVC, PTFE) negative of hair
TRIBO.lic: AlphaLab: reproduce only in whole; ordering used as fact, no table copied

NEUMANN.cite: Neumann equation of state: cos theta = -1 + 2 sqrt(gs/gl) exp(-beta (gl - gs)^2), beta = 1.247e-4 (m2/mJ)^2 (Kwok & Neumann 1999)

DELAMETTRIE07.cite: De la Mettrie R, Saint-Leger D, Loussouarn G et al. Shape variability and classification of human hair: a worldwide approach. Hum Biol 79:265 (2007); curl meter ring 0.98 cm diameter for types VII-VIII (Loussouarn follow-up, via hair.md R20)
DELAMETTRIE07.lic: paywalled; class definitions used as facts

MULBERRY.cite: Mulberry Park Silks press release (vendor-commissioned texture-analyser test, lab not named): hair tress pulled over 22 momme silk 3529 g mm vs cotton 5344 g mm (-34 %)
MULBERRY.lic: vendor page; weak evidence, ratio only used

ANON_E.cite: This lane's estimate (reason given in each src)

PHYS.cite: Standard mechanics: EI = E pi d^4/64 (ellipse I = pi a b^3/4 at equal area), J = pi d^4/32, gravity length (EI/(rho A g))^(1/3), cantilever first mode f1 = 1.875^2/(2 pi L^2) sqrt(EI/(rho A)), wave speeds sqrt(E/rho), sqrt(G/rho), capillary bridge between crossed cylinders F = 4 pi R gamma cos theta

JSCC82.cite: J Soc Cosmet Chem 33(2) (1982): hair fibre density vs relative humidity, Table V (SCC online library v033n02/39)
JSCC82.lic: free to read; numbers used as facts, text studied only
